PullRequest.Title: editor: keep wrapped Agents tab controls separate
PullRequest.Body:

Fixes #336898. Follow-up to #340635.

When Agents editor tabs wrap, Add Tab and the contextual/layout actions can occupy the same trailing area, hiding controls. This change gives the existing toolbars one positioning and measurement owner and reserves their combined width on the final visible tab item.

- Preserve horizontal scrolling when a real tab or the trailing controls cannot fit the actual wrapped viewport.
- Use the actual final Add Tab row for Connected row classification, and keep its height on the existing tab-row ramp.
- Relayout when toolbar or Add Tab menu visibility changes. Preserve nonwrapped sticky/reveal behavior and separate pinned rows.
- Preserve Connected strip-color ownership, including translucent customizations, independently of sticky positioning.
- Add production bounds/fallback regressions and real-menu header fixtures.

## Testing

1. Open an Agents window with enough file tabs to wrap; enable `workbench.editor.wrapTabs`. Confirm Add Tab, contextual actions, the separator, and layout actions remain visible and separate.
2. Repeat with default and compact tab heights, separate pinned tabs, and both high-contrast themes. Navigate the actions by keyboard.
3. Resize until Add Tab is alone on the final row. The preceding real tabs should remain upper-row pills without touching the actions.
4. Narrow the pane further, including a file tab wider than the viewport. Confirm horizontal scrolling replaces wrapping when required.
5. Turn wrapping off and confirm the normal tab/action reveal behavior remains unchanged.

Local validation:
- `./scripts/test.sh --reporter dot --run src/vs/workbench/test/browser/parts/editor/multiEditorTabsControl.test.ts --run src/vs/sessions/contrib/editor/test/browser/editorTabsLayout.test.ts --run src/vs/sessions/contrib/editor/test/browser/editor.contribution.test.ts --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/modernUI/test/browser/modernUI.contribution.test.ts` — passed.
- `npm run test-browser-no-install -- --browser chromium --browser firefox --browser webkit --run src/vs/sessions/contrib/editor/test/browser/editorTabsLayout.test.ts --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/modernUI/test/browser/modernUI.contribution.test.ts --grep 'fit and fixed tabs become upper pills|an oversized non-final fit tab|composites translucent connected strip colors only once' --reporter dot` — passed in all three engines.
- `npm run typecheck-client` — passed.
- Targeted ESLint, Stylelint, and module-layer checks — passed.
- Component Explorer before/after rendering and native Code OSS inspection — passed. Existing standard-editor scenes remain unchanged.
- The pinned four-workstream combination passed production tests, rendering, remount, keyboard, and geometry checks.

## Visual evidence

The matched fixture pair shows HC Black with identical fixed-width tabs before and after. The native Code OSS capture shows the approved compact, wrapped, HC Black layout at 144% zoom.

![After: Add Tab and both toolbars remain separate in HC Black](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/6f41ca5f-3ab1-405c-ab6e-679fff7b5e45)

Final readiness gates are complete: native visual approval, both local reviews, current-head Copilot review with no open findings, remote CI, and the exact-final cross-workstream validation passed. The corrected-identity signed head preserves the validated source tree. Collaborator approval remains a separate merge requirement.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The call path, per-frame coalescing, helper implementation, and O(N) multiplicity are explicit in repository code; only the exact millisecond impact varies by tab count and browser. Existing layout loops do not negate the newly added two computed-style reads per tab.
Findings.PerformanceResource: Per-tab DOM geometry and computed-style reads (`offsetWidth` plus two `getComputedStyle` margin reads in `getTotalWidth`)
Findings.PerformanceScaling: Each wrapped/overflowing layout adds O(number of open tabs) style measurements; resize can schedule this once per animation frame, and the default editor limit is disabled, so the cardinality is not bounded.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: Increased main-thread layout/style cost and dropped resize frames for groups with many open tabs
Findings.PreviousBehavior: The fit predicate measured only the last tab's `offsetWidth` and the toolbar width, so this portion of each layout was O(1) in the number of open tabs.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: The predicate now calls `getTotalWidth` for the last item and then for every tab to find the widest item before deciding whether wrapping is allowed.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: The added lines 2245-2247 introduce the full-tab `forEachTab` measurement loop inside `tabsFitWrapped`; the deleted predicate computed overlap from one `lastTab.offsetWidth` read.
Findings.Title: Avoid remeasuring every tab on each wrapped layout
Findings.Impact: With `workbench.editor.wrapTabs` enabled and enough tabs to overflow, every resize frame and other tab relayout scans all open tabs. Large editor groups therefore spend progressively more main-thread time measuring tab styles, making resizing and tab updates janky.
Findings.Evidence: `doLayoutTabsWrapping` runs from the animation-frame-coalesced `layout` path. When wrapping is active, or when an overflowing strip is being considered for wrapping, `tabsFitWrapped()` executes on each layout. The added `forEachTab` calls `getTotalWidth` for every tab; `getTotalWidth` reads `offsetWidth` and obtains left and right margins through two `getComputedStyle` calls. Open-editor limiting defaults to disabled, so realistic large tab sets are unbounded. The pre-diff predicate used only `lastTab.offsetWidth`.
Findings.Recommendation: Maintain the maximum required tab width when tab geometry can change (open/close, label/decorations, sizing/options), or otherwise cache per-tab total widths with those invalidations, so resize-only layouts compare a cached maximum instead of querying every tab's computed style.

Scenarios.Scenario: Resize or relayout an overflowing editor group with wrapped tabs enabled
Scenarios.CriticalPath: A resize or tab-state change calls `MultiEditorTabsControl.layout`; work is coalesced to the next animation frame, where `doLayoutTabsWrapping` must finish before the new tab geometry is painted.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Browser style/layout measurement via `offsetWidth` and two computed-style margin reads for every tab
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One last-item measurement plus one measurement per open tab on each relevant coalesced layout; `tabsFitWrapped` is normally evaluated once per layout.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The fit predicate measured only the last tab width and toolbar width, making this check constant-cardinality.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The synchronous measurements must complete in the animation-frame callback before tab wrapping and painting can settle.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of open tabs in the group after no deduplication; the default open-editor limit is disabled. With separate pinned rows, two controls can independently schedule layout work.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One pending animation-frame layout is coalesced per `MultiEditorTabsControl`; separate pinned and unpinned controls retain separate schedulers. Inside a control, all tab measurements are synchronous and serial.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Dimensions are retained, but the newly required maximum tab width is not cached. Cold and warm layouts both rescan every tab whenever the strip overflows or is wrapping; there is no coalescing across controls.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the new full-tab loop, helper implementation, layout scheduler, and pre-diff O(1) comparison are explicit.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact frame cost depends on browser style-cache behavior and tab count, but large tab groups are permitted by default and resize invokes the path at frame cadence.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable medium regression: the diff adds O(N) computed-style/geometry reads to a frame-critical layout check.

Scenarios.Scenario: Add Tab menu visibility changes as managed Files, Changes, Search, or Canvas entries change
Scenarios.CriticalPath: A relevant context-key or menu-registry change is debounced by `MenuImpl`, then updates Add Tab visibility and synchronously calls `EditorGroupView.relayout`; the group lays out its title/editor, while expensive tab DOM work remains animation-frame-coalesced.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: One configured Add Tab menu per visible editor tab control; separate pinned-row controls can each own a menu listener. Menu events are filtered to relevant context keys and registry IDs.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Menu events are debounced per menu instance. The subsequent group relayout is synchronous; local tab layouts are coalesced per control.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Menu action lists are recomputed on each relevant menu event. Visibility state is not compared before relayout, so warm events whose nonempty/empty state is unchanged still relayout, but event frequency is tied to infrequent editor/session/menu changes rather than a continuous hot path.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for the added synchronous relayout; low for a material user-visible regression because relevant events are filtered/debounced and infrequent.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Dynamic Canvas registrations can generate structural menu changes, but the menu service debounces them and repository evidence does not establish a high-frequency user path.
Scenarios.Verdict: No additional finding: the relayout preserves geometry when Add Tab visibility changes, and available evidence does not show realistic hot-path frequency.

Scenarios.Scenario: Editor and layout toolbar action visibility changes
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Action menu changes rebuild toolbar items, and the multi-tab override schedules a tab layout. Layout requests from the primary and layout toolbar update paths share the same animation-frame scheduler before painting.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of toolbar/menu changes and open tabs; toolbar width is measured once per wrapping update, while the reported full-tab scan accounts for the tab-count scaling.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Duplicate layout requests in the same frame are coalesced by `layoutScheduler`; action processing and DOM layout remain serial on the UI thread.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Toolbar actions are recreated from in-memory menus on relevant events. Layout dimensions are retained, and only one pending layout is kept; toolbar widths themselves are measured rather than cached because visibility can change.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: virtual call flow and scheduler behavior are explicit.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Extension-driven action changes vary, but scheduler coalescing prevents a same-frame burst from multiplying layouts.
Scenarios.Verdict: No separate finding: the new toolbar-triggered layout is coalesced and needed to account for changed toolbar width; its tab-scaling cost is already captured by the reported fit-scan issue.

Scenarios.Scenario: Connected/modern wrapped-tab styling and final-row classification
Scenarios.CriticalPath: During the same animation-frame tab layout, classes and row offsets are updated before paint; CSS then positions the combined toolbar and Add Tab control.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of tabs and wrapped rows. Existing per-tab class/offset loops remain; the diff adds small class toggles and one Add Tab `offsetTop` read in addition to the reported width scan.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Synchronous UI-thread DOM work, coalesced per control to one animation-frame callback.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Connected state is retained, but row geometry is intentionally recomputed after wrapping changes. There is no external cache or boundary.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for execution path and multiplicity.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The extra class toggles and single row read are minor relative to existing per-tab connected-layout loops; no independent material regression is established.
Scenarios.Verdict: No additional finding: CSS ownership changes and row classification do not independently establish actionable performance impact.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all 12 changed files and all diff pages. One introduced frame-critical repeated-work regression was reported: wrapped layout now performs computed-style/geometry reads for every open tab instead of one tab. Menu, toolbar, connected-tab, CSS, fixture, and test changes were traced; no subprocess, IPC, filesystem, database, or network boundaries are added to product scenarios, and no concrete regression fix requiring blame was established.
